elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Customer owns Type I Materials, but Type II Materials may also be created during the Service performance period and remain owned by IBM or third parties.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause does not cover all work product created for Customer; service-created Type II Materials remain owned by IBM or third parties.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all rights in deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no express assignment by IBM. The clause only states that Customer will have all right, title, and interest in Type I Materials.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all rights in work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment of work-product rights appears, and some materials created during performance are expressly categorized as IBM- or third-party-owned Type II Materials.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: Type II Materials expressly include materials that preexist the Service and in which IBM has all right, title, and interest.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables.
elements.evidence: The licence covers Type II Materials but does not expressly cover all IBM IP embedded in deliverables, and the reservation expressly excludes unlisted rights, including patent rights.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence is expressly paid-up and royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The data provision limits processing to providing the Services but does not state that Customer retains ownership or all rights in Customer Data.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own deliverables, work product, or embedded IP.
elements.evidence: Type I Materials are allocated entirely to Customer, while Type II Materials are allocated to IBM or third parties; IBM's broad Type I licence does not constitute joint ownership.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause recognizes IBM ownership of Type II Materials but does not expressly identify or allocate ownership of generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: Know-how is not identified or expressly allocated to IBM, and it cannot be assumed to fall within the undefined category of Materials.

elements.element: Customer receives rights equivalent to a licence covering the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Customer owns Type I Materials outright and receives an express licence to Type II Materials, collectively providing rights across both stated categories of Materials.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence is expressly perpetual, while Customer's ownership of Type I Materials is not time-limited.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence is expressly worldwide.

elements.element: The deliverables licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence is expressly paid-up and royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence expressly permits use, and Customer owns Type I Materials.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence expressly permits modification, and Customer owns Type I Materials.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence expressly permits sublicensing, and Customer owns Type I Materials.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its deliverables rights for its business.
elements.evidence: The Type II Materials licence expressly applies 'for Customer's business,' replacing the narrower Enterprise-only restriction.

result.reason: The redline adds the requested duration, territory, economic terms, modification, sublicensing, and business-use scope for Type II Materials, but it does not achieve the preferred ownership and assignment structure or affirm Customer's ownership of Customer Data. It also fails the fallback as written because generic tools and know-how are not expressly allocated to IBM. The data-purpose limitation is operative but is not an ownership provision. The drafting is generally coherent, though 'sublicense copies' is imprecise, paid-up and royalty-free are redundant, and the Type I/Type II framework leaves key categories dependent on classification rather than clear ownership rules.
